extracted.intended_audience: federal agency standards officials, Standards Executives, Interagency Committee members, and agency reporting staff implementing OMB Circular A-119 / P.L. 104-113
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance and required reporting items for Federal agencies under OMB Circular A-119 / P.L. 104-113 about participation in and use of voluntary consensus standards, plus the charter and functions of the Interagency Committee on Standards Policy.

rubrics_metrics.name: Number of voluntary standards bodies and employee participation
rubrics_metrics.description: Report the number of voluntary consensus standards bodies in which the agency participates, and the number of agency employees participating.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Include domestic and international bodies; count employees actively involved in standards development (not merely members of professional societies). Track turnover in participants (examples: NASA reported 148 employees in 43 bodies in FY1998, ~30% turnover).

rubrics_metrics.name: Number of voluntary consensus standards used since October 1, 1997 (per sections 11 and 12)
rubrics_metrics.description: Report the number of voluntary consensus standards the agency has used since October 1, 1997, based on the procedures in sections 11 and 12 of the Circular.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Usage may be determined by current use at installations and may lead to formal adoption. Agencies should identify standards currently used on programs as candidates for formal adoption and record adoptions (e.g., NASA adopted 414 VCS products based on current use).

rubrics_metrics.name: Identification of voluntary consensus standards substituted for government-unique standards (section 15b(7))
rubrics_metrics.description: Identify VCS that have been substituted for government-unique standards as a result of an agency review under section 15b(7) of the Circular.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Describe substitution actions and initiatives (examples: NASA participation in DoD Single Process Initiative resulted in replacement of four MIL- standards with VCS). Document reviews to identify government-unique standards that can be eliminated or replaced and timelines for completion.

rubrics_metrics.name: Evaluation of Circular A-119 effectiveness and recommended changes
rubrics_metrics.description: Provide an evaluation of the effectiveness of Circular A-119 policy and recommendations for any changes.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Include results of internal reviews and examples of policy impact (e.g., JPL eliminated 1,700 center-specific standards). Agencies may recommend additional guidance where needed (e.g., NRC asked for guidance on reporting when agencies place limitations/modifications on VCS used in regulation).

rubrics_metrics.name: Identification of instances using government-unique standards in lieu of VCS (P.L. 104-113 requirement)
rubrics_metrics.description: Identify all instances when the agency used government-unique standards instead of voluntary consensus standards; for each instance include agency rationale and the specific government-unique standard used.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Reporting may be done categorically (additions to technical standards management systems) rather than transaction-by-transaction. Explain rationales such as lack of suitable VCS, internal-use specifications, unique failure experience, or internal procedural needs (examples: NASA IT standards for internal use, NASA engineering standards from failure experience).

rubrics_metrics.name: Promotion and support of employee participation in standards development
rubrics_metrics.description: Promote and provide support for agency employee participation in voluntary consensus standards developing bodies.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide time and travel support, encourage staff contribution to standards organizations, maintain awareness initiatives to increase participation (example: NASA Technical Standards Awareness Initiative).

rubrics_metrics.name: Standards adoption process and approval chain
rubrics_metrics.description: Adoption of voluntary consensus standards should follow internal staff recommendation, steering council concurrence, and formal approval by agency-level committees/executives.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Example process: staff recommendations → Engineering Standards Steering Council concurrence → formal approval by NASA EMC and Standards Executive. Record procedural basis for each adoption.

rubrics_metrics.name: Encourage industry-developed codes/standards that can be endorsed and implemented by industry
rubrics_metrics.description: Agencies should encourage industry to develop codes, standards, and guides suitable for agency endorsement and industry implementation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This reduces need for agency-unique requirements and supports implementation by regulated entities (NRC strategy).

rubrics_metrics.name: Gathering and maintenance of information about standards and conformity activities
rubrics_metrics.description: Collect, analyze, and maintain current information about standards, product testing, quality system registration, certification, accreditation, and related rules and activities.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Information should cover activities within federal agencies, by private domestic/foreign standards bodies, and relationships among agencies and non-federal organizations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Strengthen coordination of standards-related policies among Federal agencies (Function a)
rubrics_metrics.description: Make recommendations to strengthen coordination of standards-related policies and activities among Federal agencies.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Aim for uniform policies to expedite development and adoption, and to reflect public interest.

rubrics_metrics.name: Improve efficiency of standardization efforts with U.S. private sector and international organizations (Function b)
rubrics_metrics.description: Recommend measures to improve efficiency within the Federal Government of standardization efforts with the U.S. private sector and regional/international organizations.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Focus on cooperative participation and avoiding duplication or conflicting specifications.

rubrics_metrics.name: Promote standards-related policies and personnel directory (Function c)
rubrics_metrics.description: Promote standards-related policies within the Federal Government, including maintaining a directory of personnel participating in standards activities.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Ensure consistency with statutory obligations regarding interactions with non-federal organizations and facilitate coordination by listing 'Standards Executives' and other participants.

rubrics_metrics.name: Ensure effective federal representation at significant regional and international standards meetings (Function d)
rubrics_metrics.description: Promote and ensure effective representation of the Federal Government at significant regional and international standards-related meetings and conferences.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Designate appropriate representatives to engage with SDOs and intergovernmental bodies.

rubrics_metrics.name: Promote use of internationally acceptable standards to increase trade and integration (Function e)
rubrics_metrics.description: Advocate for the use of internationally acceptable standards and related activities to foster trade and economic integration and development.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Align federal policies with international standardization where appropriate to support trade objectives.

rubrics_metrics.name: Monitor U.S. technical obligations under trade agreements (Function f)
rubrics_metrics.description: Monitor U.S. technical obligations as a signatory to WTO, US-Canada FTA, NAFTA, and other treaties on standards-related trade issues.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use monitoring to inform policy recommendations and ensure compliance with international commitments.

rubrics_metrics.name: Encourage agency strategic plans for managing use of voluntary standards (Function g)
rubrics_metrics.description: Encourage development of agency strategic plans for managing and monitoring use of voluntary standards and participation in standards-related activities.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Agency plans should address how standards are identified, adopted, tracked, and how participation is managed; Committee will assess and improve plan adequacy.

rubrics_metrics.name: Promote standards that serve national goals (metric, environmental, energy efficiency) (Function h)
rubrics_metrics.description: Promote use of standards that serve national goals related to increased use of the metric system and environmentally sound and energy efficient materials, products, systems, services, or practices.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Recommend adoption and promotion where standards can further national policy objectives.

rubrics_metrics.name: Assess and improve adequacy of agency plans and activities (Function i)
rubrics_metrics.description: Assess and improve the adequacy of agency strategic plans and standards-related activities.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide recommendations to agencies where plans or activities are insufficient to meet policy goals.

rubrics_metrics.name: Membership and representation requirements for Committee
rubrics_metrics.description: Each member agency head must ensure representation by a high level policy official (SES or higher) who serves as the agency representative on the Committee and as the 'Standards Executive'.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Representatives may designate alternates of equivalent senior status; agencies may designate experts to task groups; other federal agencies may join by application or invitation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Administrative provisions and meeting frequency
rubrics_metrics.description: NIST provides administrative arrangements; the Committee shall meet at least three times each year and may establish task groups.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: NIST responsibilities include secretarial services, meeting logistics, agendas, discussion materials, and reports.

rubrics_metrics.name: Decision-making and voting rules
rubrics_metrics.description: Decisions internal to Committee operations are by majority of those present and voting; voting on Committee business is limited to designated agency members; recommendations to the Secretary require two-thirds ratification of members present and voting; a quorum is one-half of designated members present; the Chair votes only in tie situations; dissenting positions may be recorded.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Record dissenting positions when appropriate; use majority for routine formation of task groups.

rubrics_metrics.name: Annual reporting requirement to Secretary of Commerce
rubrics_metrics.description: The Committee shall submit an annual report to the Secretary of Commerce summarizing the Committee's activity during the period and listing all recommendations formulated, to satisfy reporting requirements in OMB Circular A-119 and P.L. 104-113.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Annual report should also support members' agency reporting obligations to OMB and Congress as applicable.

rubrics_metrics.name: Estimate of annual operating cost and staffing
rubrics_metrics.description: Provide an estimate of the annual cost of operating the Committee and staff support levels.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Example: the Committee estimated annual cost at $31,000 including 0.20 staff year; agencies should budget appropriately for support.
